mechanism: Esomeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and CYP3A4, potentially increasing disulfiram levels and its hepatotoxic metabolites, while disulfiram inhibits multiple CYP enzymes including CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2E1, and CYP3A4, creating bidirectional enzyme inhibition.
action: Monitor liver function tests periodically; consider alternative PPI (pantoprazole) if hepatotoxicity concerns arise; counsel on alcohol avoidance (disulfiram requirement) and assess for increased disulfiram-related adverse effects.
